newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade data reinforces US concern-US official.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade data reinforces US concern-US official.

text.p: Japan's trade data for May, which showed that the nation's customs-cleared trade surplus more than trebled from a year earlier, reinforces U.S. concern that Japan's surplus appears to be rising again, a U.S. official in Tokyo told Reuters on Wednesday.

Japan's overall trade surplus surged for the second month in a row in May, rising 222.2 percent to 738.27 billion yen, the Finance Ministry said earlier on Wednesday. The customs-cleared trade surplus with the United States soared 93 percent in May from a year earlier to 322.87 billion yen. The figures were not seasonally adjusted.

"We still can't make any final judgment based on two or three months or even a quarter, but the numbers do reinforce our concern that the surplus appears to be climbing again and that this year there may be a significant increase in Japan's trade surplus," the official said.

The U.S. official declined to comment on what steps, if any, Japan should take to curb the rise in its surplus but said: "There is an agreement on both sides that Japan also wants to have domestic demand-led growth and has pledged to avoid a resurgence in its current account surplus. That's why we're watching this closely."
